query: What visit-note signals suggest high urgency?

per_column.name: urgency_signal_count
per_column.rationale: A count of 'urgency signals' is constructed by directly enumerating cues of the focus concept itself. It is a restatement/aggregation of urgency indicators rather than an independent predictor, so it effectively encodes the label and leaks the outcome.

per_column.name: has_critical_keywords
per_column.rationale: A binary flag for critical keywords extracted from the free-text reason_for_visit is a legitimate feature derived from the note content. It lies outside the urgency label, is knowable at intake, and plausibly carries predictive signal about urgency without being a deterministic restatement of it.

per_column.name: has_acute_presentation
per_column.rationale: Acute presentation is a clinical characteristic drawn from the note that is distinct from the urgency assignment and plausibly correlates with it. It is a valid intake-time predictor rather than a direct component of the focus variable.

per_column.name: has_severe_symptoms
per_column.rationale: Severity of symptoms is an independent, note-derived clinical signal available before any urgency determination and carries genuine predictive information about urgency without simply restating the label.

judge.rationale: Three of the four columns (critical keywords, acute presentation, severe symptoms) are legitimate note-derived predictors that are distinct from the urgency label yet plausibly correlated with it, giving real predictive leverage. However, urgency_signal_count is essentially a tally of urgency cues and effectively restates/leaks the focus. The set has moderate genuine utility, tempered by overlap among the severity flags and one leaking column.
